rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The file's one `##` heading, 'Two frontiers' (L3), is a catalogue-entry-style label naming its subject (no verb, no assertion) — squarely inside the rule's own NOT-violation carve-out ('catalogue entries naming their subject: Ralph, The numbers, Verification, named'), not a claim like 'Passing is not proof'. This is deliberate, not an omission: the maintainer watch-for (L27) reads 'Don't answer the two frontiers. They are the arc's open questions,' and the backing block's stance (L47-50) states 'holds: nothing, by design ... two open questions and one recognition line' and names the failure mode this file guards against as 'a future editor helpfully answering one of the two questions.' A heading that asserted a claim about the frontiers would itself be that failure mode. Label, not claim, is the correct shape here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bullet 1 (L5, 'The model's frontier moves without you. Every release, it can do more.') introduces the first frontier — no earlier line in this 8-line body to restate. Bullet 2 (L6, 'Your frontier is what you have expressed. It moves when you write, and only then.') is not doctrine restatement of bullet 1: it names the CONTRASTING mechanism (automatic vendor-side movement vs. authored-only movement), the load-bearing point the piece exists to make. Bullet 3 (L7) converts bullets 1-2 into two open questions rather than restating them verbatim — that conversion is this lecture's actual payload per the backing block ('two open questions and one recognition line'), not a closing koan restating the header or a '**The point:**' line (there is neither in this file). No self-referential design commentary anywhere (no line talks about the training's own pedagogy). None of the three low-value classes present.
